program_narrative: Program DB2CONN is a DB2 connection manager subprogram. The caller passes a request area (LS-DB2-REQUEST) holding a 4-character function code, a database name, a plan name, a return code and error information, and the program returns with GOBACK. Function 'CONN' connects to the requested database, retrying up to WS-MAX-RETRIES (initial value 3) times and calling the external program DELAY with DB2-RETRY-WAIT between failed attempts; each failure records the SQLCODE and an error message and sets return code 12. Function 'DISC' commits the work and resets the connection when the program believes it is connected, returning 0 on success or 8 with the SQLCODE and an error message on failure. Function 'STAT' probes the connection by selecting CURRENT SERVER and returns 0 when active or 4 with an error message when not. Any other function code sets error text 'Invalid function code', return code 12 and calls the external error program ERRPROC with ERR-MESSAGE. The plan name is moved to WS-PLAN-NAME but not used by any SQL statement; SQLCODE comes from the DB2 precompiler and has no registered Field ID.

-- Entry: caller passes db2_request (LS-DB2-REQUEST: function code, database name, plan name, return code, error info) (PROCEDURE DIVISION USING, line 46)
SELECT CASE requested_function (LS-FUNCTION)
  WHEN 'CONN' (FUNC-CONN):
    CALL 1000-connect
  WHEN 'DISC' (FUNC-DISC):
    CALL 2000-disconnect
  WHEN 'STAT' (FUNC-STAT):
    CALL 3000-check-status
  ELSE:
    SET error_text (ERR-TEXT) = 'Invalid function code'
    CALL 9000-error-routine
END SELECT
RETURN to caller  -- GOBACK

paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SET connection_state = 'N'  -- SET WS-DISCONNECTED TO TRUE: mark as not connected
CLEAR retry_count (WS-RETRY-COUNT)  -- initialise to zero
SET ws_db_name = request_db_name (LS-DB-NAME)
SET ws_plan_name = request_plan_name (LS-PLAN-NAME)
WHILE NOT (connected (WS-CONNECTED) OR retry_count >= max_retries (WS-MAX-RETRIES)) DO  -- PERFORM UNTIL, condition tested before each pass
  SQL CONNECT TO database :ws_db_name
  IF SQLCODE = 0 THEN  -- CHECK SQLCODE
    SET connection_state = 'Y'  -- SET WS-CONNECTED TO TRUE
    SET return_code (LS-RETURN-CODE) = 0
  ELSE
    INCREMENT retry_count BY 1
    CALL 1100-handle-conn-error
  END IF
  IF retry_count < max_retries AND NOT connected THEN
    CALL program DELAY
      PASSING: db2_retry_wait (DB2-RETRY-WAIT, copybook DBPROC)
      -- external subprogram: wait before the next connection attempt (behaviour not traced here)
  END IF
END WHILE

annotations.note: Inline PERFORM UNTIL (lines 69-88). WS-MAX-RETRIES has initial VALUE 3 and is never changed, so at most 3 CONNECT attempts are made.
WS-PLAN-NAME is set from the request but not referenced by any SQL statement in this program.
DELAY is a static external CALL, not a paragraph; calls_made_ids keeps null IDs for it. DB2-RETRY-WAIT has initial VALUE 100 in copybook DBPROC.
Each failed attempt sets LS-RETURN-CODE to 12 and an error message (1100-HANDLE-CONN-ERROR). After the last failed attempt the loop ends with those values; the caller sees return code 12.

paragraphs.name: 2000-DISCONNECT
pseudocode: SQL COMMIT WORK  -- commit the current unit of work
SQL CONNECT RESET  -- disconnect from DB2
IF SQLCODE = 0 THEN  -- CHECK SQLCODE (of the CONNECT RESET; the COMMIT result is not checked)
SET connection_state = 'N'  -- SET WS-DISCONNECTED TO TRUE
END IF  -- not connected: nothing is done and LS-RETURN-CODE is left as passed by the caller
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
IF connected (WS-CONNECTED) THEN
  SQL COMMIT WORK  -- commit the current unit of work
  SQL CONNECT RESET  -- disconnect from DB2
  IF SQLCODE = 0 THEN  -- CHECK SQLCODE (of the CONNECT RESET; the COMMIT result is not checked)
    SET connection_state = 'N'  -- SET WS-DISCONNECTED TO TRUE
    SET return_code (LS-RETURN-CODE) = 0
  ELSE
    SET error_sqlcode (LS-SQLCODE) = SQLCODE
    SET error_message (LS-ERROR-MSG) = 'Error disconnecting from DB2'
    SET return_code = 8
  END IF
END IF  -- not connected: nothing is done and LS-RETURN-CODE is left as passed by the caller

annotations.note: WS-CONNECTION-STATE is a WORKING-STORAGE item with no VALUE clause; it is set only by earlier calls (CONN or STAT) in the same run unit. Whether it holds 'Y' on a DISC call depends on the caller's call sequence.

paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SQL SELECT CURRENT SERVER FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1 INTO :ws_db_name  -- probe whether a DB2 connection is active
IF SQLCODE = 0 THEN  -- CHECK SQLCODE
  SET connection_state = 'Y'  -- SET WS-CONNECTED TO TRUE
  SET return_code (LS-RETURN-CODE) = 0
ELSE
  SET connection_state = 'N'  -- SET WS-DISCONNECTED TO TRUE
  SET error_sqlcode (LS-SQLCODE) = SQLCODE
  SET error_message (LS-ERROR-MSG) = 'DB2 connection not active'
  SET return_code = 4
END IF
